dhp334:2: his craving grows like a creeping vine.
dhp334:3:
He runs now here
& now there,
dhp334:4:
as if looking for fruit:
a monkey in the forest.
dhp335:3: your sorrows grow like wild grass
dhp336:1: If, in the world, you overcome
dhp336:2: this uncouth craving, hard to escape,
dhp336:4:
like water beads off
a lotus.
dhp337:1: To all of you gathered here
dhp337:4:
–as when seeking medicinal roots, wild grass–
by the root.
dhp337:5:
Don’t let Mara cut you down
–as a raging river,
dhp338:1:
If its root remains
undamaged & strong,
dhp338:2:
a tree, even if cut,
will grow back.
dhp338:3:
So too if craving-obsession
is not rooted out,
dhp339:2: flowing to what is appealing, are strong:
dhp339:4: carry him, of base views, away.
dhp340:1: They flow every which way, the streams,
dhp340:2:
but the sprouted creeper stays
in place.
dhp340:3: Now, seeing that the creeper’s arisen,
dhp340:4:
cut through its root
with discernment.
dhp341:2: are the joys of a person.
dhp341:3:
People, bound by enticement,
looking for ease:
dhp342:2:
hop round & around
like a rabbit caught in a snare.
dhp342:4:
they go on to suffering,
again & again, for long.
dhp343:1:
Encircled with craving,
people hop round & around
dhp343:2: like a rabbit caught in a snare.
dhp343:4:
should dispel craving,
should aspire to dispassion
for himself.
dhp344:1:
Cleared of the underbrush
but obsessed with the forest,
dhp344:2:
set free from the forest,
right back to the forest he runs.
dhp344:4:
set free
who runs right back to the same old chains!
dhp345:1:
That’s not a strong bond
–so say the enlightened–
dhp345:2: the one made of iron, of wood, or of grass.
dhp345:3:
To be smitten, enthralled,
with jewels & ornaments,
dhp346:1:
that’s the strong bond,
–so say the enlightened–
dhp346:2:
one that’s constraining,
elastic,
hard to untie.
dhp346:3:
But having cut it, they
–the enlightened–go forth,
dhp346:4:
free of longing, abandoning
sensual ease.
dhp347:1:
Those smitten with passion
fall back
into a self-made stream,
dhp347:2: like a spider snared in its web.
dhp347:3: But, having cut it, the enlightened set forth,
dhp347:4:
free of longing, abandoning
all suffering & stress.
dhp348:1: Gone to the beyond of becoming,
dhp348:4:
you don’t come again to birth
& aging.
dhp349:1:
For a person
forced on by his thinking,
dhp349:2:
fierce in his passion,
focused on beauty,
dhp349:4:
He’s the one
who tightens the bond.
dhp350:1:
But one who delights
in the stilling of thinking,
dhp350:2:
always
mindful
cultivating
a focus on the foul:
dhp350:3:
He’s the one
who will make an end,
dhp350:4: the one who will cut Mara’s bond.
dhp351:3:
he has cut away
the arrows of becoming.
dhp351:4: This physical heap is his last.
dhp353:2:
with regard to all things,
unadhering.
dhp353:3:
All-abandoning,
released in the ending of craving:
dhp353:4:
having fully known on my own,
to whom should I point as my teacher?
dhp354:1:
A gift of Dhamma conquers
all gifts;
dhp354:2:
the taste of Dhamma,
all tastes;
dhp354:3:
a delight in Dhamma,
all delights;
dhp354:4:
the ending of craving,
all suffering
& stress.
dhp355:1:
Riches ruin the man
weak in discernment,
dhp355:2:
but not those who seek
the beyond.
dhp355:3:
Through craving for riches
the man weak in discernment
dhp355:4:
ruins himself
as he would others.

So what’s given to those
free of passion
dhp357:3:
So what’s given to those
free of aversion

So what’s given to those

So what’s given to those
